title: Spiced Potato and Pea Flatbreads
subtitle: Indian stuffed flatbreads with samosa-spiced filling
excerpt: Spiced potato and pea filling wrapped inside a simple unleavened dough and cooked in a dry frying pan. All the flavours of a samosa in a flatter, quicker format. Good for lunch or a light supper.
sourceNotes: Stuffed flatbreads are common across India in forms like aloo paratha and keema paratha. This version takes the classic samosa filling and uses it as a paratha-style stuffing.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the filling up to a day ahead and keep in the fridge.

content.text: Keep the filling dry. If it has too much moisture, the dough will tear when you roll it. Mash the potato well and make sure the peas are drained and patted dry.

items.prepNote: 2 tbsp for dough, 2 tbsp for frying

content.text: Make the dough. Combine the flour with 2 tablespoons of oil and a pinch of salt. Add 150ml of warm water gradually, mixing until a soft dough forms.
Knead for 3 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest while you make the filling.
Mix the mashed potato with the peas, ginger, and all the spices. Season well with salt.
Divide the dough into 8 equal balls.
Flatten each ball, add a spoonful of filling to the centre, then fold the dough up around it and pinch to seal.
Gently roll each stuffed ball out to a circle about 18cm across. Use plenty of flour on the surface.
Heat a dry frying pan over a medium-high heat.
Cook each flatbread for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and slightly charred in spots.
Brush with a little oil as it comes off the pan. Keep warm in a low oven while you cook the rest.

items.symptom: Filling bursts through the dough when rolling.
items.cause: Too much filling was added or the dough is too thin at the edges.
items.fix: Use less filling and roll gently from the centre outward.

items.symptom: Flatbreads are stiff instead of soft.
items.cause: Dough was not kneaded enough or was over-floured.
items.fix: Knead for a full 3 minutes and keep extra flour minimal.
